transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi Dr. Smith. I... I came in because I keep hearing these voices. They're as clear as somebody standing right in my little studio. Which, honestly, I need to get out of that place. The landlord, Frank, he never fixes the radiator, and I have to buy those plastic sheets for the windows to keep the draft out. You know the ones you shrink with a hair dryer? My hair dryer actually sparked and died right in my hand last Tuesday. Scared me half to death. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices. Yeah, they just keep saying my name and telling me my work is being judged. I'm a personal care aide, and I work hard for my clients, you know? I don't need to be judged. But they say it even when the house is completely quiet and nobody is there. Just empty. Kind of like Mrs. Miller's house—she's one of my clients, bless her heart, she barely talks anymore, just sits in her recliner and watches her daytime stories all day. I usually make her a turkey sandwich around noon, but anyway, yeah... the voices are just there when nobody else is.
Have you been feeling unusually low, hopeless, or perhaps the complete opposite—like you have a massive amount of energy or need very little sleep—during the time you've been hearing these voices?

Well, the sleep thing... yeah, actually. Not too long ago I was only sleeping maybe two, maybe three hours a night. I just didn't need it. I had all this energy because I was pushing these big art-and-care plans I came up with. I figured out how to combine watercolor painting with mobility exercises for my clients, and it was going to be huge. I even went down to the craft store to buy all these special brushes. They have that coupon, you know, the one on the phone app? But my phone is so old it wouldn't load at the register and the cashier kept tapping her long acrylic nails on the counter. Tap, tap, tap. It was so rude. I should have said something to her manager, but I was in such a rush. 

But what you asked... right, the voices. Yes, even when I was barely sleeping and working on all those big plans, I was still hearing the voices right there in my studio. And it was weird because I also started feeling like certain people were watching my work. Like they were keeping tabs on what I was doing in there. Which is just... I mean, my window just faces the alley where the stray cats get into the recycling bins. I tried leaving tuna out for them once, but Frank got mad and said it brings raccoons. Have you ever seen a raccoon up close? They have little hands like tiny people. It's really unsettling when you catch them just standing on their back legs staring at you in the dark.
Are there times when you are feeling like your normal self, sleeping normally, and not having all those big plans, but the voices are still there?

Yeah... yeah, actually there was. After all that energy kind of crashed out of me, I went back to sleeping my regular hours. Which is a miracle, honestly, because my mattress is just terrible. I got it from this thrift store down on 4th street, and the guy swore up and down it was deep-cleaned, but it has this one spring that pokes me right in the left hip. I have to fold up this thick quilt under the fitted sheet just to get comfortable. My grandmother made that quilt, actually, it has all these little embroidered birds on it. She loved birds. She used to have this canary named Peaches that would sing every single time the telephone rang. It was one of those old rotary phones, so it was real loud... 

But, oh, right, you were asking about feeling normal. So, yeah, my energy dropped back down, I wasn't doing the big plans anymore, just sleeping my regular hours. But the voices... they didn't stop. For several weeks after that, they just kept right on going. The voices, and that whole feeling that people were tracking my work and judging what I was doing. It just kept going for weeks even though I felt normal otherwise. It's so exhausting, you know? Kind of like when you're trying to write out your grocery list and the TV is on too loud in the background. I usually just buy the same things anyway, like milk and those little cans of fruit cocktail. Do you like the ones with the cherries? I always save the cherry for last, but sometimes they don't even put one in the can, which just feels like a rip-off.

You mentioned the voices and the feeling of being watched continued for several weeks after your energy levels and sleep returned to normal; could you tell me exactly how long that period of being 'normal' with the voices lasted?

Well, it was definitely for several weeks. Like, a good solid chunk of time where I was just feeling pretty regular, you know, not running around with all those big plans and I was sleeping my normal hours again despite that awful mattress. But the voices, and that whole feeling that people were tracking my work and judging me... that just kept right on going the whole time. It was so frustrating. 

Speaking of tracking things, I started trying to track my miles for work because I have to drive to all my different clients. I got this little notebook from the dollar store, it has a picture of a golden retriever on the front. I love dogs. My neighbor when I was a kid had a golden retriever named Buster, and he would always dig under the fence and steal our garden hose. Just the hose! He'd drag it into his yard and chew on the brass fitting. My dad would get so mad, his face would turn this shade of purple, like a plum. We had a plum tree in the backyard, actually, but the plums were always sour. I tried making jam out of them once, but I think I put too much pectin in it because it turned into this giant rubbery block in the jar. You could literally bounce it on the counter. But anyway, yeah, the voices and the tracking feeling lasted for several weeks even when I was otherwise feeling fine.
About how many months in total have you been experiencing these voices and the feeling that people are tracking your work?

Well, it's been about nine months total. Nine whole months of hearing them and feeling like my work is being watched and judged like that. It's a long time to feel that way, you know? Nine months. That's how long my sister was pregnant with my nephew, obviously, but it felt like she was pregnant forever. She craved the weirdest things, too, like pickles wrapped in American cheese and dipped in mustard. I tried a bite once just to see, and honestly, it wasn't terrible, but the mustard kept dripping on my shirt. It was one of my favorite shirts, too, this soft yellow cotton one I got at a yard sale for fifty cents. The lady having the sale had this huge collection of vintage salt and pepper shakers. Hundreds of them, all lined up on these little wooden shelves. She had a pair that looked like two little alligators hugging. I almost bought them, but I don't really use salt. Too much sodium makes my ankles swell up, especially when I'm on my feet all day with my clients. But yeah, nine months of all this.
Looking back at these nine months, how much of that time would you say you were feeling that high energy and needing very little sleep?

Well, looking at the whole nine months... I'd say for most of that stretch, I was either totally wound up with all those big plans and getting hardly any sleep, just nonstop activity, you know? Or I was kind of coming down from that but still not really back to myself yet. So most of the time was spent like that. Just going and going. 

I was doing so much, actually, I even started reorganizing my client Mrs. Higgins' entire house. I'm a personal care aide, so I'm really just supposed to help with her meals and getting dressed, but I just had so much energy to burn. She has this massive collection of porcelain dolls in her living room. I took every single one out to dust them. They have those painted eyes that look like they're staring right through you, which always gives me the shivers. One of them was wearing this tiny little velvet dress, a really deep burgundy color. It looked exactly like a dress my mother wore to my cousin's wedding back in the eighties. That wedding was at this fancy golf club, and they served these little crab puff appetizers that gave my uncle food poisoning. He was stuck in the bathroom for the entire reception. They had to cut the cake without him, which was a shame because it was a beautiful cake, three tiers with those little silver candy beads on it. I always worry about breaking a tooth on those beads, though, they're practically solid glass.
Aside from the period where you were feeling very energetic and sleep-deprived, were there any other times during these nine months where you felt depressed, sad, or hopeless for a few weeks or more?

No, I haven't really felt sad or hopeless like that. It was mostly just the high energy and then the voices. I don't really get depressed, just tired sometimes. Speaking of tired, I've been trying to drink more tea instead of coffee because coffee makes my stomach do backflips. I bought this chamomile and lavender blend from the health food store. The girl working there had the most incredible hair, it was dyed bright teal, like the color of a swimming pool on a really sunny day. It made me think of the community pool we used to go to when I was a teenager. They had this high diving board that I was always too scared to jump off of. My brother dared me to do it once, for five dollars, but I just stood up there shaking until the lifeguard told me to climb back down the ladder. It was so embarrassing. Everyone was watching. Five dollars was a lot of money back then, too. I could have bought three whole cassette tapes at the mall with that. I used to love going to the music store, just flipping through the tapes and looking at the album covers. The smell of the plastic cases always reminds me of being fifteen. But no, no depression or anything like that for me.
During those nine months, were there any times when you felt like people were tracking your work or judging you even when you weren't feeling that high energy or those big plans?

Yeah, actually, there was. Even after all that crazy energy finally wore off and I started sleeping regular hours again, I still felt it. For several weeks, honestly. The voices were still there, and I was still absolutely sure people were tracking everything I did at work, judging me. It didn't stop just because I was sleeping. I remember because I tried buying these blackout curtains to help me sleep better when I finally could sleep. They were supposed to be navy blue, but when I took them out of the package, they were more of an eggplant color. Eggplant is such a strange vegetable, don't you think? It's so spongy. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he grows them in his backyard. He brought me a huge one last summer. I tried to make eggplant parmesan, but I didn't salt it first to draw the moisture out, so the breading got all soggy. It was a disaster. I ended up giving it to my dog, Buster. Buster will eat anything, though. Once he ate a whole pack of sugarless gum I left in my purse, and I had to rush him to the emergency vet. That vet clinic always smells like wet fur and rubbing alcohol. They had this poster on the wall showing the anatomy of a flea, which is just disgusting when you really look at it up close. But yeah, the tracking and the voices, they definitely kept going for weeks even when I wasn't feeling all wound up.

I remember because I tried buying these blackout curtains to help me sleep better when I finally could sleep. They were supposed to be navy blue, but when I took them out of the package, they were more of an eggplant color. Eggplant is such a strange vegetable, don't you think? It's so spongy. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he grows them in his backyard. He brought me a huge one last summer. I tried to make eggplant parmesan, but I didn't salt it first to draw the moisture out, so the breading got all soggy. It was a disaster. I ended up giving it to my dog, Buster. Buster will eat anything, though. Once he ate a whole pack of sugarless gum I left in my purse, and I had to rush him to the emergency vet. That vet clinic always smells like wet fur and rubbing alcohol. They had this poster on the wall showing the anatomy of a flea, which is just disgusting when you really look at it up close. But yeah, the tracking and the voices, they definitely kept going for weeks even when I wasn't feeling all wound up.

inference.note: The patient reports a primary period of mood symptoms (mania) accompanied by psychosis, followed by a period of at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. This pattern is characteristic of schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent auditory hallucinations and delusions (being tracked/judged) for a duration of nine months. These psychotic symptoms were present for several weeks in the absence of mood symptoms (the 'normal' period described), meeting the criteria for Schizoaffective disorder, specifically the manic type, as the psychotic symptoms were prominent during the period of elevated mood and activity, but also occurred independently.

confirmed_symptoms: excessive involvement in activities with high potential for painful consequences (e.g., reorganizing client's house)

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have been present for approximately nine months total, with psychotic symptoms persisting for several weeks independent of the mood episode.
